target_reasoning: Average Speed chosen over Congestion Level / Travel Time Index / Road Capacity Utilization because those columns are heavily saturated at their max value (43.5%/58.5%/73.7% of rows respectively), making them poor continuous regression targets. Average Speed is continuous, unclipped, and converts directly to edge travel time for routing (time = distance / speed).
sequence_length_reasoning: Dataset is DAILY and IRREGULARLY sampled per road (gaps of 1-10 days between consecutive observations for the same road; no fixed 5-minute or hourly frequency exists in this data). Sequences are therefore built from the previous N RECORDED observations for a road, not N fixed time units. seq_len=10 was chosen as a balance: large enough to give the LSTM meaningful history, small enough that even the road with the fewest observations (275) still yields hundreds of usable training sequences.

split.method: chronological, global (70/15/15) by target-row date, no shuffling

architecture: LSTM(64, return_sequences=True) -> Dropout(0.2) -> LSTM(32) -> Dropout(0.2) -> Dense(16, relu) -> Dense(1)
